meta.title: Awesome Grok Bot
meta.description: Specialists and teams you put into Grok Bot. Copy setup text from a listing and paste it in. You can also hand off from Hermes or OpenClaw.

what.a: A sponsor-free Grok Bot directory. Copy specialist or team setup text and paste it into Grok Bot. It is not an official xAI product.

importer.q: Does Grok Bot have an official importer?
importer.a: No. There is also no public API to create Bots or write memory. This site is a catalog plus a Hermes and OpenClaw skill.

updates.q: Where can I see Grok Bot updates and new features?
updates.a: The changelog at getgrokbot.com/changelog is a hand-curated timeline of Grok Bot updates — each entry has a date, a short note, and a link to the official xAI post or doc.

inside.q: Can I run Claude Code, Codex, or OpenClaw inside Grok Bot?
inside.a: Yes — Grok Bot has its own computer, so you can tell it to install coding agents like Claude Code or Codex and drive them. getgrokbot.com/install has paste-ready prompts. Logins stay human.

copy.q: How do I use a listing?
copy.a: Copy the setup text from a detail page and paste it into Grok Bot. Start with one Chief. Login and 2FA stay human.

migrate.q: How do I move from Hermes or OpenClaw?
migrate.a: Paste one line from getgrokbot.com/migrate into the agent you already use. That agent reads the skill and hands over packets. Keys and .env stay behind.

free.a: The directory and migrate skill are free and MIT. Grok Bot app access is an xAI or Cursor plan.

migrate.hubTitle: From a previous agent into Grok Bot
migrate.hubLead: Paste one line into the agent you already use. It loads the skill and moves the profile into Grok Bot. This site does not write to Grok. First Bot is one Chief. You only handle login walls.
migrate.ruleMemory: Memory is preview-then-confirm. Daily notes and DREAMS are a working layer, so they stay off the queue unless you opt in.
migrate.ruleRoutines: A skill is how; a routine is when. Official order: do the task once → save as a skill → then schedule a routine. Cap 50 routines per Bot. Duplicate Bot does not copy learned memory.
migrate.ruleSecrets: .env, auth.json, apiKey, botToken, SecretRef values, and key-looking strings are always stripped. Sessions, state.db, and transcripts are not memory.
migrate.hermesLead: Install the skill in Hermes and say migrate. It reads SOUL, USER, MEMORY, skills, and cron, then hands packets across.
migrate.hermesPageLead: Paste the one-liner into Hermes or install the skill. If it can operate the Grok app it pastes packets; if not, it gives you Copy one packet at a time. Keys stay behind.
migrate.openclawLead: Put the skill in OpenClaw and say migrate. It reads a zip or AGENTS, HEARTBEAT, and openclaw.json.
migrate.openclawPageLead: Paste the one-liner into OpenClaw or drop SKILL.md into skills/. Keys stay behind. hermes claw migrate is optional tidy only.

accept.hermes: zip/tar.gz profile, or SOUL.md, USER.md, MEMORY.md, memories/*, skills/*/SKILL.md, cron.
accept.openclaw: zip, or SOUL.md, AGENTS.md, USER.md, MEMORY.md, memory/*.md, HEARTBEAT.md, openclaw.json, cron/jobs.json, skills. Legacy clawdbot/moltbot names work.

migrate.includeOptional: Add {count} daily notes / DREAMS to the queue (off by default)
migrate.honesty: This does not move API keys or run {source} on Grok. It hands the next Grok Bot the next piece. Memory, skill, and routine packets are Copy-only into chat. We cannot write xAI memory APIs.
migrate.saveListingHint: Opens Submit with the profile packet.

handover.createBotBody: In the Grok Bot app, make one Bot. Leave setup blank. Name it. That Bot is the handoff desk.
handover.copyPromptBody: It has operating rules, packet order, and login-wall handling. Use it whole.
handover.pasteSourceTitle: Paste it into the agent you already use
handover.pasteSourceBody: Hermes or OpenClaw. Tell it the empty Bot’s name. Let it print an inventory before it drives anything.
handover.gatesBody: The prompt stops Grok Bot. You type passwords, SSO, and 2FA. It does not start the next packet until you say continue.
handover.gatePassword: Passwords are typed by a human. Never taken from a file or from memory.
handover.gateSso: Company SSO, SAML, and Okta stay with the human at the IdP.
handover.gateOauth: If OAuth scopes look too broad, it asks before continuing.
handover.gateSecond: 2FA, passkeys, magic links, and CAPTCHAs are human-only.
handover.gateShare: If Grok Bots share a computer, logins are shared. It says that once.
handover.exportLead: A zip or SOUL.md can still be split into packets here. The default path is the prompt above.

playbook.banner: This URL’s phase only. Do not skip. Do not save, schedule, or cut over before the human marks Done.

playbook.lockedBody: Finish the previous phase before using Copy here.
playbook.goldLead: Write 3–5 before you start. They are the only cutover score. Memory-restore rate is not.
playbook.goldNeed: Fill 3–5 gold tasks before you start.
playbook.startDisabled: Start stays off until gold tasks are ready.
playbook.limitDuplicate: Duplicate Bot does not copy learned memory, history, or attachments.
playbook.limitComputer: Bots share one computer. Sessions are shared.
playbook.limitTeach: Teach a task is a browser demo, about 10 minutes.

playbook.inventoryOpenclaw: Inventory: zip first. SOUL, AGENTS, USER, MEMORY, memory/*, HEARTBEAT, openclaw.json, cron/jobs.json, skills.
playbook.tidyOpenclaw: Optional: tidy locally with hermes claw migrate. The default path is an OpenClaw zip. Do not use --migrate-secrets.
playbook.factsNote: Standing facts live in FACTS.md. Quote the file. “Remember these” with no file is a fail.
playbook.routinesLead: Name a saved skill only. Empty means hold. Source cron off; this side Test run only.
playbook.leftoverLead: won't-port, HEARTBEAT, archived memory. Sign them. Do not silent-delete.
playbook.appendixLead: The phase Copy is the default. Use this whole prompt only if {source} loses the order.

0.title: Inventory
0.actor: {source} scans and prints the table in chat. The human only confirms a backup.
0.fail: Keys left in the body, or calling a session DB memory.

1.title: Chief
1.actor: The human creates one Grok Bot Chief and pastes the profile.
1.fail: Creating specialist Bots or a Nexus here.

2.title: Fact file
2.actor: The human puts FACTS.md on the shared computer. The Chief quotes it.
2.fail: “Remember these” with no file. Honcho or full sessions.

3.title: Skills
3.actor: Human and Chief. Run each priority skill once, then save.
3.fail: Promoting an unrun skill to a routine.

4.title: Routines
4.actor: Human and the owning Bot (Chief by default). Source cron off.
4.fail: Both sides live. A routine with no skill. More than 50.

5.title: Connectors
5.actor: Only the human types logins. The site is a checklist.
5.fail: Uploading secret files. Assuming split Bots isolate sessions.

6.title: Cutover
6.actor: The human checks gold tasks and signs leftovers.
6.fail: Cutting over because memory looks the same. Source still on.

0.listOk: The inventory list matches. A session DB is not memory.

1.neverDo: The description has the role and never-do.

2.factsFile: FACTS.md is on the shared computer.

3.wontPortListed: won't-port items are on the leftover list.

4.testRun: A Test run passed. Test run is real.
4.underFifty: This Bot has 50 routines or fewer.

5.pluginsLinked: Plugins needed by gold tasks are connected.
5.allowlistOnly: Only allowlisted files were uploaded. No secret files.

6.sourceArchived: The source is off and archived.

steps.accessBody: Early beta ships with SuperGrok Heavy, Cursor Ultra, and Cursor Teams Premium. Enterprise is a waitlist. If the app will not open, start with the plan.
steps.installBody: Desktop (macOS) or iOS. The same thread continues on both. Bots keep a cloud computer, so work does not stall when you close the laptop.
steps.createBody: Name it. Setup can be short. Do not build a whole team on day one. Pick a daily job: inbox or a morning brief.
steps.setupBody: Copy a listing from the directory. It already has the job, the bar for good work, the never-do list, and a first task.
steps.taskBody: Send, delete, and pay stay off. Read the result. Widen the scope only after that looks right.
steps.loginBody: When a Bot reaches mail, CRM, or calendar, a login wall appears. Passwords, SSO, 2FA, and CAPTCHAs stay with you. Sessions live on the computer. If Bots share that computer, they share sessions.
steps.skillTitle: Show it once, then save a skill
steps.skillBody: Let it watch a workflow, then save how. Routines (when) wait until the skill exists. Cap 50 routines per Bot. Duplicate Bot does not copy learned memory.
steps.teamTitle: Then add a Nexus or an Orchestrator
steps.teamBody: Put a router (Nexus) or a sequencer (Orchestrator) in so you are not the paste middleman. Specialists keep one lane. They pass work in a group chat and pull you in for judgment only.

install.title: Run coding agents inside Grok Bot
install.lead: Give Grok Bot a coding agent on its own cloud computer. Copy one prompt, let the Bot install it, then keep every login in human hands.
install.note: This is community guidance, not official xAI guidance. Never hand credentials or API keys to an agent; Grok Bot should stop at every login wall and ask you to take over.
install.hardRule: Never type credentials or API keys. Stop at every login or API-key step and ask the human to do it. Logins stay human.
